lead: A UAV (uncrewed aerial vehicle), or drone, is a small aircraft that flies a planned mission and carries a camera or scanner. A drone survey takes many overlapping photos, matches the same ground points in them, and builds a map and an elevation model. It exists because one pilot can cover a site in minutes at centimetre-level detail. Users apply it to topographic mapping, construction progress, landslide and flood mapping, and agriculture.
prereq: You need: GPS and GNSS: principles and positioning methods for positions, liDAR and laser scanning for point clouds, and remote sensing for image basics.

blocks.text: A multirotor has four or more rotors. It takes off and lands vertically, hovers, and flies slowly. A survey multirotor typically flies 20 to 40 minutes on one battery and suits sites of about 10 to 50 ha, single structures and close inspection. A fixed-wing drone has wings and must keep moving. For its size it generally carries more payload and flies much longer, so it covers hundreds of hectares in one flight and suits long strips, but it cannot hover and needs a launch and landing area. A hybrid VTOL (vertical take-off and landing) combines both.

items: RGB camera: cheap photos for an orthomosaic and surface model.
Multispectral camera: several bands for crop stress and vegetation indices.
LiDAR scanner: direct ranges and a point cloud that can see ground under gaps in trees.
GNSS tag: each photo gets a position; RTK (real-time kinematic) GNSS gives 1–3 cm.
GCP (ground control point): a marked point on the ground with known coordinates, used to check or correct the model.

blocks.text: GSD (ground sample distance) is the ground size of one image pixel. A smaller GSD means finer detail. Use flying height above ground, not above mean sea level.

blocks.where: GSD is ground sample distance in metres per pixel; p is pixel pitch (pixel size) in metres; H is flying height above ground in metres; f is focal length in metres.

blocks.text: Overlap is the shared part of two photos. Along-track overlap is between successive photos in a strip; side overlap is between adjacent strips. Survey flights use about 70–80% along-track and 60–70% side overlap. Overlap creates common points for matching.

With 80% along-track overlap, each new photo adds 20% new ground. Spacing = footprint × (1 − overlap fraction). Number of images = strip length ÷ spacing, rounded up, + 1. The footprint is the ground length covered by one photo: the number of pixels along that side times the GSD.
SfM (structure from motion) is a photogrammetric method that recovers 3D structure and camera positions from overlapping images.

items: Detect keypoints (corners and blobs) in every image.
Match the same keypoint across overlapping images.
Calibrate the camera: focal length, principal point, lens distortion.
Build tie points: matched points seen in many images.
Run bundle adjustment: solve camera positions and 3D point positions together by minimising reprojection error.
Build a dense cloud from all pixels, then a mesh and products.

blocks.text: Products: an orthomosaic is a seamless top-down map made from rectified images. A DEM (digital elevation model) is an elevation grid. A DSM includes buildings and trees; a DTM is bare ground after ground points are classified. Resolution is close to GSD. High overlap and sharp photos matter more than a high megapixel count for matching. RTK positions help bundle adjustment, but GCPs still catch drift. The dense cloud carries colour from RGB images or direct elevation from LiDAR. Some syllabi call this drone photogrammetry.

In India, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) regulates drones. Outline: register the drone, fly only in permitted zones, and hold a remote pilot certificate. Red zones are no-fly; airports and sensitive areas need clearance. Keep line of sight and follow height limits. Permits depend on weight class and zone; green zones need less paperwork. Do not fly over people or moving traffic without permission.

Uses: topographic mapping, construction monitoring, landslide and flood mapping, agriculture, and stockpile volumes. A construction team flies weekly and compares DEMs to measure cut and fill. A landslide map uses a DSM before and after rain. A farm uses multispectral images to spot water stress. For setting out, see construction surveys and setting out.

examples.question: A drone camera has pixel size 2.4 µm, focal length 8.8 mm and an image of 5472 × 3648 pixels, flown with the short side along track. It flies at 120 m above ground. Find the GSD and the ground footprint. For a 3.0 km strip with 80 % along-track overlap, find the photo spacing and the number of images; with 70 % side overlap, find the spacing between strips.
steps: Convert units: p = 2.4 µm = 2.4 × 10⁻⁶ m; f = 8.8 mm = 0.0088 m; H = 120 m.
Footprint along track = 3648 × 0.03273 = 119.4 m; across track = 5472 × 0.03273 = 179.1 m.
Intervals in 3000 m = 3000 ÷ 23.88 = 125.6, rounded up to 126; images = 126 + 1 = 127.
examples.answer: GSD 3.27 cm; footprint 119.4 m × 179.1 m; photos every 23.9 m, 127 images for the strip; strips 53.7 m apart.

traps: Using flying height above mean sea level instead of above ground. A site at 500 m elevation with 120 m above ground is 620 m above sea level.
Treating GSD as contour interval. GSD is pixel size on the ground; contour interval is vertical spacing between contours.
Reading 80% overlap as 80% new area. It leaves 20% new ground, so spacing is 0.20 × footprint.
Assuming RTK GNSS removes the need for GCPs. GCPs check datum, camera model and systematic drift.
Mixing the orthomosaic with a single photo or with the DEM. The orthomosaic is a 2D map; the DEM is elevation.

quiz.q: State one difference between a multirotor and a fixed-wing survey drone.
quiz.a: A multirotor takes off vertically and can hover; a fixed-wing cannot hover and needs forward motion for lift.

quiz.q: Name three common drone payloads for surveying.
quiz.a: RGB camera, multispectral camera, and LiDAR scanner.

quiz.q: Why do drone surveys use 70–80% along-track overlap?
quiz.a: Overlap gives many common points in successive photos, so SfM can match features, solve camera positions and build a dense cloud.

quiz.q: What is a ground control point (GCP) and why is it used?
quiz.a: A GCP is a marked ground point with known coordinates. It checks or corrects the model's datum, scale and systematic error.

quiz.q: A camera has pixel size 3.0 µm and focal length 10 mm. The drone flies 100 m above ground. Find the GSD in centimetres.
A landslide site is partly under trees. Explain why a LiDAR payload can be better than an RGB camera for the ground surface.
quiz.a: RGB depends on daylight and visible texture; trees hide the ground. LiDAR measures ranges directly and some pulses pass through gaps, so ground points can be classified under canopy.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern drones use RTK or PPK (post-processed kinematic, where positions are corrected after the flight) to tag each image to 1–3 cm, and UAV LiDAR is used under canopy. Terrain-aware flight keeps constant height above ground, so GSD stays constant. Research uses AI change detection between flights for construction and landslides. Search for UAV LiDAR survey, PPK drone mapping, structure from motion bundle adjustment, and DGCA Digital Sky. Beyond-line-of-sight operations are expanding.
